slides.heading: Sequential Execution
slides.body: Sequential Execution is part of Introduction to Python and Output. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Sequential Execution
slides.body: Python normally runs statements from top to bottom. This order is called sequential execution, and changing the order can change the result.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Sequential execution is like lining up at a cashier. The first person is served first, then the next, then the next.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Write one clear instruction at a time. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so order and spelling matter.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Print First, Second, and Third on separate lines in the correct order.
slides.hint: Use three print() calls. The first written line prints first.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Write three print statements that display Start, Work, and Finish on separate lines.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
